title: Design a Global POI Nearest-Neighbor Platform
prompt: Design a global read-heavy point-of-interest catalog with hundreds of millions of records and sub-100ms nearby top-K queries, category/rating filters, edits, bulk updates, and bounded eventual consistency. Cover spatial indexing, exact distance ranking, hotspot handling, cache invalidation, regional routing, and failure behavior.

response.placeholder: Use a spatial index only to find candidates; explain how exact top-K remains correct at cell boundaries.
response.reference_answer:
## Read path
Store canonical POIs separately from query projections. Map a query to hierarchical spatial cells, route to regional replicas, apply category/rating filters, calculate exact distance, and merge local top-K results. A fixed containing cell plus eight neighbors is not sufficient for exact nearest-K: expand rings until every unvisited cell's distance lower bound exceeds the current Kth candidate, or enumerate all cells intersecting a radius.

## Writes and freshness
Send idempotent edits and bulk jobs to durable shard leaders. Version rows, asynchronously update cell postings, and advance a cell cache epoch so stale keys miss. Bulk jobs are partitioned/rate-limited to protect reads; communicate the local/global freshness bound.

## Scale and failures
Use geohash-like logical prefixes with virtual shard mapping and deeper splits for dense cities. Route users to healthy regions; replicate durable logs across regions and serve declared stale data during failover. Track candidate fan-out, hot cells, projection lag, cache age, and exact-result latency.

## Progressive Hints
1. Coordinates need exact post-filtering.
2. Hot cities defeat a fixed physical prefix shard.
3. TTL alone is not update correctness.
